[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Thomas was born before 1742.

== Research Notes ==
A possible identification concerns Glasco, Dublin watch and clock maker. A watch and clock maker advertising only as Glasco moved from Christ-Church-lane to 20 Ormond Quay, near the market. Original notices inspected on 5 October 1779 and 4 April 1780 state the same move.<ref>Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Tuesday, 5 October 1779, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050086381/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Thursday, 7 October 1779, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050086390/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Tuesday, 12 October 1779, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050086411/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Tuesday, 21 December 1779, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050048548/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Thursday, 23 December 1779, p.4; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050048569/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Saturday, 5 February 1780, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050048725/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Saturday, 19 February 1780, p.4; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050048807/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Saturday, 26 February 1780, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050048846/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Saturday, 4 March 1780, p.3; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050048882/ record]; Public Register, or Freeman's Journal, Tuesday, 4 April 1780, p.4; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050049040/ record].</ref> All sixteen original advertisements were inspected and saved; they repeat the same address change from 5 October 1779 through 4 April 1780. No first name or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Glasco, Dublin watch and clock maker. Under Robbery And Reward, the shop of Messrs Peter and Semple at 108 Grafton Street was entered and stolen watches listed. One is a gold double-cased watch marked “Glasco and Son, Dublin.” The stolen watch bears the number 3203.<ref>Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-11, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050127957/ record]; Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-13, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050128500/ record]; Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-15, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050129060/ record]; Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-18, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050129538/ record].</ref> This is a maker/firm mark on a watch listed among stolen property in a robbery notice. The issue dates the printed notice, not manufacture or continuous business activity; “and Son” does not prove named father and son. The watch is not established as made in the existing watchmaker’s shop, and no individual or family identity follows. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Possible Thomas Glascoe of Tinicum Island ===
Thomas reports $115 stolen from his Tinicum Island house on 31 March 1799; the April 9 notice is reprinted on April 11.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/586542475/ Aurora General Advertiser, 1799-04-09, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/586542512/ Aurora General Advertiser, 1799-04-11, p.1].</ref>

Thomas is the subscriber and reported theft victim; William Steel is the alleged thief. The reports do not name Thomas’s family or connect him with the Dublin Glasco households.

This may concern [[Glasco-173]]. Chronologically compatible Thomas Glasco profile; no Tinicum or Delaware identification is established.
